Close Update: Bullish Jobs Report and Fed Chair Powell Unleash Blistering Risk Rally January 04, 2019, 04:39:41 PM EDT By MT Newswires, MT Newswires Shutterstock photo
Powered by a bullish labor market report and assurances by the Fed chairman that Wall Street is factored into interest rate decisions, stocks closed with significant gains and at their highest levels in ten days. Led by gains in semiconductor and software stocks, the Nasdaq Composite closed more than 4% higher.
Even accounting for Thursday's Apple-fueled meltdown, the major market indices all closed the week with impressive gains. Although Apple ( AAPL ) lost more than 3% in value this week, the Nasdaq took the lead with a 2.3% gain over last Friday's close. The S&P 500 followed with a gain of 1.8% while the Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 1.6% from the prior week's close.
Stocks were gaining altitude before this morning's data as progress towards US/China trade negotiations and Beijing's efforts to pump up liquidity by lowering the reserve ratio requirement fueled 2% gains across most of Asia and a 1% gain in Dow futures.
Any lingering worries about a recession were extinguished by a 312,000 gain in non-farm payrolls coupled with a 0.4% increase in average hourly earnings. Coupled with Powell's remarks mid-morning, a furious risk-rally was unleased across all sectors of the market tech and industrial stocks outperforming.
Investors' appetite for risk drove Treasury yields sharply higher as the 10-year note cheapened 11 basis points, its biggest one-day gain in two years. Gold was down $7 and lower for the first time in six days. Despite broad-based pressure on metals, copper closed in the green after a string of losses as easing recessionary risks propped up the price of the industrial metal.
